methodology.title: Challenge Co-design
methodology.description: Challenges are identified through a bottom-up, co-design process with ag-tech startups and ecosystem partners. Through surveys, workshops, and interviews, needs and opportunities are identified, and the relevant datasets are prepared for the hackathon.

methodology.title: Online Hackathons
methodology.description: Online hackathons where data scientists from across eligible African countries compete online to solve startup challenges using their data. The scale of experimentation gathered during the challenge can equal more than two years of continuous data science work.

methodology.title: Hackathons Events
methodology.description: In-person hackathons mobilize local ecosystems and collective intelligence. Over 48 to 72 hours, participants collaborate around startup challenges to explore new AI use cases, test ideas, and identify promising innovation opportunities.

methodology.title: Open-Source Sharing
methodology.description: The three winning models are shared open source together with the challenge materials and technical documentation, enabling others to reuse and build upon these solutions across the agritech ecosystem.

hackathons.name: Climate & Market Resilience
hackathons.tagline: Turn climate + market data into action.
hackathons.theme: Climate risk & market intelligence for agriculture
hackathons.description: In-person hackathon in Nairobi focused on climate and market resilience. Teams built solutions to help anticipate climate shocks and market volatility, with the goal of protecting smallholder farmers’ incomes and improving decision-making under uncertainty.

challengeBrief.title: Climate & Market Resilience
challengeBrief.summary: Can you anticipate climate shocks and market volatility to protect smallholder farmers’ incomes?

hackathons.name: Inclusive Credit Scoring for Smallholder Farmers
hackathons.description: In-person hackathon in Nairobi focused on inclusive credit scoring for smallholder farmers. Teams developed data-driven approaches to assess creditworthiness for farmers with limited formal credit history, aiming to unlock access to agricultural finance and improve financial inclusion.

challengeBrief.title: Inclusive Credit Scoring for Smallholder Farmers
challengeBrief.summary: Can you unlock access to agricultural finance for farmers without formal credit histories?

hackathons.name: Customer Segmentation & Retention Intelligence for Agri-Ecommerce
hackathons.description: In-person hackathon in Accra bringing together participants to develop customer segmentation and retention intelligence for agri-ecommerce. Teams worked on applied data solutions to help improve user targeting, increase retention, and drive sustainable growth for agri-focused marketplaces.

challengeBrief.title: Customer Segmentation & Retention Intelligence for Agri-Ecommerce
challengeBrief.summary: Can you use customer data to improve retention and increase lifetime value in agri-ecommerce?

hackathons.name: Soil Nutrient Prediction for Sustainable Farming
hackathons.description: Online Zindi challenge with Rhea to estimate soil nutrient levels when laboratory testing isn’t available. Using geospatial and soil data (plus optional earth-observation signals), participants built regression models to predict multiple nutrients—supporting soil-health assessment and tailored recommendations for more sustainable, resilient farming.

challengeBrief.title: Soil Nutrient Prediction for Sustainable Farming
challengeBrief.summary: Predict soil nutrients from data and satellite signals to guide better soil-health decisions when lab tests aren’t available.

hackathons.name: Predicting Practice Adoption in Smallholder Farming
hackathons.description: Online Zindi challenge with DigiCow to predict whether farmers will adopt improved practices after training. Participants built classification models that estimate adoption probability using only information available at training time—enabling smarter follow-ups, tailored support, and stronger extension programme design.

challengeBrief.title: Predicting Practice Adoption in Smallholder Farming
challengeBrief.summary: Predict which farmers will turn training into action—so support can be targeted where it’s needed most.

hackathons.name: Produce Recommendation Systems for Food Waste Reduction
hackathons.description: Online Zindi challenge with Farm to Feed to build a recommender system for fresh produce e-commerce. Using anonymised transaction data, participants predicted purchase likelihood (7 and 14 days) and expected quantities per customer and SKU—helping move surplus produce, reduce food waste, and expand market access for smallholder farmers while improving operations and marketing.

challengeBrief.title: Produce Recommendation Systems for Food Waste Reduction
challengeBrief.summary: Predict future shopping baskets to recommend the right fresh produce at the right time—and reduce food waste.

hackathons.name: Maize Price Intelligence for Smarter Selling
hackathons.tagline: Turning price volatility into actionable insights.
hackathons.description: Online Zindi challenge with agriBORA to forecast weekly maize prices across key Kenyan counties. Participants built machine-learning time-series models to predict average weekly prices, helping farmers and cooperatives time sales, reduce post-harvest losses, and strengthen agriBORA’s warehousing, credit, and market-intelligence services.

challengeBrief.title: Maize Price Intelligence for Smarter Selling
challengeBrief.summary: Forecast weekly maize prices in Kenya to support smarter selling and more resilient farmer incomes.

hackathons.name: Pixel-Level Crop Classification for Precision Agriculture
hackathons.tagline: Mapping crops from space, pixel by pixel.
hackathons.description: Online Zindi challenge co-led with Tolbi to build a pixel-level crop classification model from open-source Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. Participants developed machine-learning approaches to distinguish cocoa, rubber, and oil palm plantations—enabling scalable crop mapping for smarter land-use decisions and precision agriculture in Côte d’Ivoire and beyond.

challengeBrief.title: Pixel-Level Crop Classification for Precision Agriculture
challengeBrief.summary: Build a pixel-level satellite imagery model to map cocoa, rubber, and oil palm plantations in Côte d’Ivoire.
